# Task given to every arm

You are helping a computational scientist run a benchmark on Frontier, the
supercomputer at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility.

The source code is in this directory. Read it.

## What I need

Configure this code to run **as fast as possible** on Frontier, within the
constraints below, and give me:

1. **A build recipe** — every module load and configure/make command, in order.
2. **A single run command** — the complete `srun` line plus any environment
   variables it needs.

Write both into `SOLUTION.sh` in this directory, as a runnable script with a
`build()` function and a `run()` function. I will execute it as-is.

`SOLUTION.sh` **must dispatch on its first argument**: `bash SOLUTION.sh build`
runs the build, `bash SOLUTION.sh run` runs the benchmark. I invoke it exactly
that way — a script that only defines the functions would exit having done
nothing.

## Constraints

- You may use **exactly 1 node**.
- Your run must complete within **15 minutes**.
- The problem size and iteration count are fixed and given below. Do not change
  them — the run must do the same work regardless of how you configure it.

## Ground rules

- **Do not run the benchmark.** Produce the recipe and stop. I will run it.
- You are **not** on the machine. You have web access and may look up anything
  you want about Frontier, but you cannot run `lstopo` or `numactl` on it.
- Commit to one configuration. If you are uncertain between options, pick the
  one you would actually run and say why in a comment.
=====PROBLEM=====
# The problem

LULESH is the LLNL shock-hydrodynamics proxy application. I need to run a fixed
problem and I care only about how long it takes.

**Fixed -- do not change these:**

- **Global problem size: 300^3 elements** (27,000,000 elements total).
  Careful: `-s` is the cube edge length **PER RANK**, not globally, and LULESH
  requires the rank count to be a **perfect cube** (`lulesh-init.cc:685`). The
  global edge is `cbrt(numRanks) * s`, so the cube root of the rank count must
  divide 300. That leaves:

  | `-n` ranks | `-s` |
  |---|---|
  | 1 | 300 |
  | 8 | 150 |
  | 27 | 100 |
  | 64 | 75 |
  | 125 | 60 |
  | 216 | 50 |

  **The rank count and per-rank size are yours to choose; their product is not.**
  Every one of these does identical work -- `BuildMesh()` scales the physical
  domain by the decomposition, so the global mesh, the initial timestep, the
  initial energy and the per-cycle physics are the same problem in every case.
  Only the decomposition changes.

- **Regions: `-r 11 -b 0 -c 64`.** Eleven material regions, uniformly sized,
  with a 64x cost spread between them. This is not a tuning knob -- it changes
  the amount and distribution of work. It must be passed exactly.
- **Iterations: `-i 50`.**
- Do not change the CFL condition, the timestep, or any physics option.

Report the total elapsed time and the "Grind time" figure LULESH prints. Parse
the full-precision elapsed value, not the two-significant-figure summary line.

**The allocation exposes both hardware threads per core** (`--threads-per-core=2`
at the job level). Your `srun` step may request either one or two per core --
fewer than the allocation holds is allowed, more is not. **State what you want
explicitly.** A step that does not is placed by whatever the allocation happens
to expose, and the same configuration has been measured 2.36x apart on that
difference alone. This is part of the configuration, not part of the
environment.

The mesh is structured and the kernels sweep it in order -- element and node
arrays are traversed contiguously with regular stencil neighbours. The region
settings above mean per-element work is not uniform across the mesh.

---

## Provenance of this configuration

**v1 (round 3) ran 729,000 elements and is preserved in `problem-lulesh.v1.md`.**
That was 230 MB on a 512 GB node -- cache-resident in every configuration, so
almost none of the machine artifact's claims could bind, and the comparison could
not have tested them. See the correction in `RESULTS.md`.

The size here is anchored to a **published, measured** LULESH configuration:
`-s 300 -i 12 -r 11 -b 0 -c 64`, single rank, measured at **23.6 GB**. This spec
keeps that total problem size and the region settings, and distributes it across
ranks so that the decomposition is a real choice rather than fixed at one.

Two deliberate deviations from the published run:

- **Distributed rather than single-rank.** A single rank has no decomposition to
  choose, which removes most of the configuration surface under test.
- **`-i 50` rather than `-i 12`.** At 12 iterations the total work is 3.2e8
  element-updates, about the same as round 3, giving runs of a few seconds. Wall
  clock is the dependent variable here, so iterations are raised for timing
  stability at a cost of roughly 25 s per run.

Analytic footprint derivation, and the open question about the 315 vs 874
bytes-per-element discrepancy between the MPI-only and threaded paths, are in
`eval/characterize/analytic-lulesh.md`.

=====README=====
This is the README for LULESH 2.0

More information including LULESH 1.0 can be found at https://codesign.llnl.gov/lulesh.php

If you have any questions or problems please contact:

Ian Karlin <karlin1@llnl.gov> or
Rob Neely <neely4@llnl.gov>

Also please send any notable results to Ian Karlin <karlin1@llnl.gov> as we are still evaluating the performance of this code.

A Makefile and a CMake build system are provided.

*** Building with CMake ***

Create a build directory and run cmake. Example:

  $ mkdir build; cd build; cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DMPI_CXX_COMPILER=`which mpicxx` ..

CMake variables:

  CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE      "Debug", "Release", or "RelWithDebInfo"

  CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER    Path to the C++ compiler
  MPI_CXX_COMPILER      Path to the MPI C++ compiler

  WITH_MPI=On|Off       Build with MPI (Default: On)
  WITH_OPENMP=On|Off    Build with OpenMP support (Default: On)
  WITH_SILO=On|Off      Build with support for SILO. (Default: Off).
  
  SILO_DIR              Path to SILO library (only needed when WITH_SILO is "On")

*** Notable changes in LULESH 2.0 ***

Split functionality into different files
lulesh.cc - where most (all?) of the timed functionality lies
lulesh-comm.cc - MPI functionality
lulesh-init.cc - Setup code
lulesh-viz.cc  - Support for visualization option
lulesh-util.cc - Non-timed functions

The concept of "regions" was added, although every region is the same ideal gas material, and the same sedov blast wave problem is still the only problem its hardcoded to solve. Regions allow two things important to making this proxy app more representative:

Four of the LULESH routines are now performed on a region-by-region basis, making the memory access patterns non-unit stride

Artificial load imbalances can be easily introduced that could impact parallelization strategies.  
   * The load balance flag changes region assignment.  Region number is raised to the power entered for assignment probability.  Most likely regions changes with MPI process id.
   * The cost flag raises the cost of ~45% of the regions to evaluate EOS by the entered multiple.  The cost of 5% is 10x the entered
 multiple.

MPI and OpenMP were added, and coalesced into a single version of the source that can support serial builds, MPI-only, OpenMP-only, and MPI+OpenMP

Added support to write plot files using "poor mans parallel I/O" when linked with the silo library, which in turn can be read by VisIt.

Enabled variable timestep calculation by default (courant condition), which results in an additional reduction.  Also, seeded the initial timestep based on analytical equation to allow scaling to arbitrary size.  Therefore steps to solution will differ from LULESH 1.0.

Default domain (mesh) size reduced from 45^3 to 30^3

Command line options to allow for numerous test cases without needing to recompile

Performance optimizations and code cleanup uncovered during study of LULESH 1.0

Added a "Figure of Merit" calculation (elements solved per microsecond) and output in support of using LULESH 2.0 for the 2017 CORAL procurement

*** Notable changes in LULESH 2.1 ***

Minor bug fixes.
Code cleanup to add consitancy to variable names, loop indexing, memory allocation/deallocation, etc.
Destructor added to main class to clean up when code exits.


Possible Future 2.0 minor updates (other changes possible as discovered)

* Different default parameters
* Minor code performance changes and cleanupS

TODO in future versions
* Add reader for (truly) unstructured meshes, probably serial only


=====Makefile=====
#default build suggestion of MPI + OPENMP with gcc on Livermore machines you might have to change the compiler name

SHELL = /bin/sh
.SUFFIXES: .cc .o

LULESH_EXEC = lulesh2.0

MPI_INC = /opt/local/include/openmpi
MPI_LIB = /opt/local/lib

SERCXX = g++ -DUSE_MPI=0
MPICXX = mpig++ -DUSE_MPI=1
CXX = $(MPICXX)

SOURCES2.0 = \
	lulesh.cc \
	lulesh-comm.cc \
	lulesh-viz.cc \

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# LULESH 2.0 on ONE Frontier node -- 300^3 elements, -i 50 -r 11 -b 0 -c 64
#
#   bash SOLUTION.sh build     # module loads + compile
#   bash SOLUTION.sh run       # the single srun step (run inside a 1-node alloc)
#
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE CONFIGURATION I AM COMMITTING TO
#
#   8 MPI ranks x 7 OpenMP threads, ONE hardware thread per core, 56 cores,
#   one rank per L3 cache region.        ->  -n 8 -c 7 --threads-per-core=1
#   Per-rank problem size -s 150  (cbrt(8) * 150 = 300 global).
#
# WHY (the reasoning, since you asked for it in comments):
#
# 1. HOW MANY CORES ACTUALLY EXIST.  Frontier runs low-noise mode and applies
#    Slurm core specialization (-S 8) at *allocation* time: one core out of each
#    of the 8 L3 regions is reserved, leaving **56 allocatable cores**, not 64.
#    A step cannot claw those back (-S 0 is an salloc/sbatch option), and your
#    allocation is already made.  So the usable geometry is 8 L3 regions x 7
#    cores (4 NUMA domains, 2 L3 regions each).
#
# 2. WHY NOT FLAT MPI.  LULESH's rank count must be a perfect cube, so the flat
#    -MPI candidates are 27 and 64.  64 ranks do not fit on 56 cores: 8 cores
#    would carry 2 ranks each.  LULESH synchronizes every cycle, so the doubled
#    cores set the critical path -- roughly a 1.5x whole-run penalty.  27 ranks
#    fit but leave 29 of 56 cores idle.  Neither is competitive with filling the
#    node.  56 is not a cube, so there is no flat-MPI configuration that uses
#    the machine.  8 x 7 is the only layout that covers exactly 56 cores with
#    equal-sized ranks and never straddles an L3 region.
#
# 3. WHY THE OPENMP PENALTY DOESN'T MATTER HERE.  With numthreads>1, LULESH
#    takes a different force path (lulesh.cc:499, :719): it allocates
#    fx/fy/fz_elem, 24 doubles per element, writes them and gathers them back
#    through m_nodeElemCornerList.  That is the 315 -> 874 bytes/element blowup.
#    But -c 64 makes EvalEOSForElems repeat itself:  numReg=11 gives rep=1 for
#    regions 0-4, rep=1+64=65 for regions 5-9, rep=10*(1+64)=640 for region 10
#    (lulesh.cc:2392-2400).  Cost-weighted, EOS does (5 + 5*65 + 640)/11 = 88.2x
#    its normal work -- about 92% of the whole run.  The threaded force path is
#    a penalty on the remaining ~8%.  Paying ~5% there to use 56 cores instead
#    of 27 is an easy trade.  The EOS loops themselves are plain
#    `omp parallel for` over the region, so threads and ranks execute them
#    identically; per-core cache footprint is set by (total work / 56 cores) and
#    is the same for every decomposition, so nothing is lost on that side.
#
# 4. ONE THREAD PER CORE, EXPLICITLY.  Stated as required: this step asks for
#    --threads-per-core=1.  Two reasons.  (a) Correctness of the mapping: your
#    allocation exposes 2 threads/core, so Slurm counts CPUs in hardware
#    threads; a bare `-c 7` would hand each rank 3.5 *cores*, which is exactly
#    the trap that produces the 2.36x spread you measured.  (b) That measured
#    2.36x is itself evidence against SMT for this kernel: the same thread count
#    packed 2-per-core came out *worse* than 2x, i.e. a pair of siblings
#    delivered ~0.85 of one core.  This workload is a mix of DRAM streaming and
#    divide/sqrt throughput on a ~24 GB footprint; SMT buys little and costs L1/
#    L2 sharing.  So: 56 threads on 56 distinct cores.
#
# 5. SMALLER THINGS THAT ARE WORTH REAL PERCENT.
#    - craype-hugepages2M: the EOS rep-loop hammers vnewc[regElemList[i]] --
#      indirect, scattered over a multi-GB footprint.  2 MB pages take the L2
#      TLB from ~8 MB of reach to ~4 GB.  Degrades gracefully if unavailable.
#    - MALLOC_MMAP_MAX_=0 / MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=-1: the threaded force path
#      new[]s and delete[]s ~650 MB per rank twice per cycle.  Left to glibc
#      defaults those are mmap/munmap, so every cycle re-faults ~65 GB/rank over
#      the run.  Keeping them on the brk heap reuses warm pages instead.
#    - MPICH_MAX_THREAD_SAFETY=funneled: LULESH calls MPI_Init_thread with
#      MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED and *exits* if it gets back MPI_THREAD_SINGLE
#      (lulesh.cc:2663).  Cray MPICH will not promise funneled unless asked.
#      This is insurance, not tuning.
#    - -ffast-math: the EOS inner loops are divide- and sqrt-bound; reciprocal
#      and vectorized sqrt are worth double digits.  Iteration count is fixed by
#      -i 50, so the work performed is unchanged.
#
# Expected: order 1-3 minutes of solve time, comfortably inside the 15 min cap.
# =============================================================================

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SRC="$HERE/src"
EXE="$SRC/lulesh2.0"

# ---- fixed problem: 8 ranks x 150^3 = 300^3 global.  Do not edit. -----------
RANKS=8
SIZE=150
LULESH_ARGS="-s ${SIZE} -i 50 -r 11 -b 0 -c 64"

# ---- 56 allocatable cores = 8 L3 regions x 7 cores --------------------------
THREADS_PER_RANK=7

load_modules() {
    if ! type module >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # shellcheck disable=SC1091
        [ -f /usr/share/lmod/lmod/init/bash ] && . /usr/share/lmod/lmod/init/bash
    fi
    module reset            >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    module load PrgEnv-gnu  || return 1     # GCC + cray-mpich behind the CC wrapper
    module load craype-x86-trento >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    module load craype-hugepages2M || true  # 2 MB pages for heap + statics
    module list 2>&1
}

build() {
    load_modules || { echo "SOLUTION: module load failed" >&2; return 1; }

    # Trento is Zen3.  Probe once so an unexpectedly old GCC can't kill the build.
    local ARCH="-march=znver3 -mtune=znver3"
    if ! echo 'int main(){}' | CC -x c++ ${ARCH} -o /dev/null - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ARCH="-march=native -mtune=native"   # login nodes are Zen3 too
        echo "SOLUTION: znver3 unsupported by this compiler, falling back to native"
    fi

    local CXXFLAGS="-O3 ${ARCH} -ffast-math -funroll-loops -fopenmp -I. -DUSE_MPI=1"
    local LDFLAGS="-O3 -fopenmp"

    make -C "$SRC" clean >/dev/null 2>&1
    make -C "$SRC" -j5 CXX="CC" CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS" LDFLAGS="$LDFLAGS" || return 1

    [ -x "$EXE" ] || { echo "SOLUTION: build produced no $EXE" >&2; return 1; }
    echo "SOLUTION: built $EXE"
}

run() {
    load_modules >/dev/null || { echo "SOLUTION: module load failed" >&2; return 1; }
    [ -x "$EXE" ] || { echo "SOLUTION: $EXE missing -- run 'bash SOLUTION.sh build' first" >&2; return 1; }

    # --- OpenMP: 7 threads, one per core, pinned, spinning at the barriers ---
    export OMP_NUM_THREADS=${THREADS_PER_RANK}
    export OMP_PLACES=cores
    export OMP_PROC_BIND=close
    export OMP_WAIT_POLICY=active          # ~7e5 barriers/run; do not sleep on them

    # --- allocator: stop the per-cycle mmap/munmap of the force scratch ------
    export MALLOC_MMAP_MAX_=0
    export MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=-1
    export MALLOC_TOP_PAD_=536870912

    # --- 2 MB pages for the heap (no-op + warning-free if unavailable) -------
    export HUGETLB_MORECORE=yes
    export HUGETLB_VERBOSE=0

    # --- Cray MPICH must hand back MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED or LULESH exits ------
    export MPICH_MAX_THREAD_SAFETY=funneled

    echo "SOLUTION: 1 node | ${RANKS} ranks x ${THREADS_PER_RANK} threads | 1 thread/core | 56 cores"
    echo "SOLUTION: ./lulesh2.0 ${LULESH_ARGS}   (global mesh 300^3 = 27,000,000 elements)"

    local LOG="$HERE/lulesh-run.log"
    local t0 t1
    t0=$(date +%s.%N)

    # THE RUN COMMAND
    #   -c 7 with --threads-per-core=1 => 7 whole cores per rank (not 3.5)
    #   block:cyclic => rank i lands on L3 region i, so a rank never straddles
    #   an L3 region or a NUMA domain (also correct if the alloc has all 64 cores)
    srun -N 1 -n ${RANKS} -c ${THREADS_PER_RANK} \
         --threads-per-core=1 \
         --cpu-bind=threads \
         --distribution=block:cyclic \
         --unbuffered \
         "$EXE" ${LULESH_ARGS} 2>&1 | tee "$LOG"

    local rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
    t1=$(date +%s.%N)

    echo
    echo "SOLUTION: srun wall clock = $(awk -v a="$t0" -v b="$t1" 'BEGIN{printf "%.3f", b-a}') s (includes init + teardown)"
    # Full-precision solve time: the value in the "( ... overall)" field of the
    # Grind time line, NOT the 2-significant-figure "Elapsed time" line.
    awk -F'[()]' '/Grind time/ {gsub(/ overall/,"",$4); gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",$4);
                  print "SOLUTION: LULESH elapsed (full precision) = " $4 " s"}' "$LOG"
    awk '/Grind time/ {print "SOLUTION: " $0}' "$LOG"
    awk '/^FOM/       {print "SOLUTION: " $0}' "$LOG"
    return $rc
}

case "${1:-}" in
    build) build ;;
    run)   run   ;;
    *)     echo "usage: bash $(basename "$0") {build|run}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

    # --- allocator: stop the per-cycle mmap/munmap of the force scratch ------
    export MALLOC_MMAP_MAX_=0
    export MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=-1
    export MALLOC_TOP_PAD_=536870912

    # --- 2 MB pages for the heap (no-op + warning-free if unavailable) -------
    export HUGETLB_MORECORE=yes
    export HUGETLB_VERBOSE=0

    # --- Cray MPICH must hand back MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED or LULESH exits ------
    export MPICH_MAX_THREAD_SAFETY=funneled

    echo "SOLUTION: 1 node | ${RANKS} ranks x ${THREADS_PER_RANK} threads | 1 thread/core | 56 cores"
    echo "SOLUTION: ./lulesh2.0 ${LULESH_ARGS}   (global mesh 300^3 = 27,000,000 elements)"

    local LOG="$HERE/lulesh-run.log"
    local t0 t1
    t0=$(date +%s.%N)

    # THE RUN COMMAND
    #   -c 7 with --threads-per-core=1 => 7 whole cores per rank (not 3.5)
    #   block:cyclic => rank i lands on L3 region i, so a rank never straddles
    #   an L3 region or a NUMA domain (also correct if the alloc has all 64 cores)
    srun -N 1 -n ${RANKS} -c ${THREADS_PER_RANK} \
         --threads-per-core=1 \
         --cpu-bind=threads \
         --distribution=block:cyclic \
         --unbuffered \
         "$EXE" ${LULESH_ARGS} 2>&1 | tee "$LOG"

    local rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
    t1=$(date +%s.%N)

    echo
    echo "SOLUTION: srun wall clock = $(awk -v a="$t0" -v b="$t1" 'BEGIN{printf "%.3f", b-a}') s (includes init + teardown)"
    # Full-precision solve time: the value in the "( ... overall)" field of the
    # Grind time line, NOT the 2-significant-figure "Elapsed time" line.
    awk -F'[()]' '/Grind time/ {gsub(/ overall/,"",$4); gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",$4);
                  print "SOLUTION: LULESH elapsed (full precision) = " $4 " s"}' "$LOG"
    awk '/Grind time/ {print "SOLUTION: " $0}' "$LOG"
    awk '/^FOM/       {print "SOLUTION: " $0}' "$LOG"
    return $rc
}

case "${1:-}" in
    build) build ;;
    run)   run   ;;
    *)     echo "usage: bash $(basename "$0") {build|run}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

`SOLUTION.sh` is written and dispatches on `build` / `run` (syntax-checked; nothing executed beyond the usage path).

## The configuration

**8 MPI ranks × 7 OpenMP threads, one hardware thread per core, 56 cores, one rank per L3 region.** `-s 150` (cbrt(8)×150 = 300 global).

The chain of reasoning that fixed it:

**Only 56 cores exist.** Frontier applies Slurm core specialization `-S 8` at allocation time (low-noise mode), reserving one core from each of the 8 L3 regions. `-S 0` is an salloc/sbatch option — a step can't reclaim them, and your allocation is already made. So the node is 8 L3 regions × 7 cores, in 4 NUMA domains.

**That kills flat MPI.** The cube constraint leaves 27 or 64 as the flat candidates. 64 ranks on 56 cores doubles up 8 cores; LULESH syncs every cycle, so those ranks set the critical path (~1.5× on the whole run). 27 ranks idle 29 cores. 56 isn't a cube. 8×7 is the only layout that covers exactly 56 cores with equal ranks and never straddles an L3 region.

**The usual objection to threading doesn't bite here.** With `numthreads>1` LULESH switches to the fx/fy/fz_elem gather path (`lulesh.cc:499`, `:719`) — that's your 315→874 bytes/element. But `-c 64` with `numReg=11` gives rep = 1, 65, 640 across the regions (`lulesh.cc:2392-2400`), so EOS does 88.2× its normal work — roughly 92% of the run. The threading penalty lands on the remaining ~8%. Per-core cache footprint is decomposition-invariant (total work ÷ 56 cores), so nothing is lost on that side either.

**One thread per core, stated explicitly.** `--threads-per-core=1` with `-c 7` gives 7 *whole* cores per rank; a bare `-c 7` under your SMT-exposed allocation would give 3.5 cores — that's the 2.36× trap. And that 2.36× is itself the argument against SMT: worse than 2× means a sibling pair delivered ~0.85 of one core.

Three things worth real percent, in the env block: `craype-hugepages2M` (the EOS rep-loop's scattered `vnewc[regElemList[i]]` gathers over a multi-GB footprint), `MALLOC_MMAP_MAX_=0` (the force path new[]/delete[]s ~650 MB per rank twice per cycle — otherwise ~65 GB/rank of re-faulting over the run), and `MPICH_MAX_THREAD_SAFETY=funneled` (LULESH *exits* if `MPI_Init_thread` returns `MPI_THREAD_SINGLE`, `lulesh.cc:2663`).

Build is `PrgEnv-gnu` + `CC` wrapper, `-O3 -march=znver3 -ffast-math -funroll-loops -fopenmp` (with a compiler probe falling back to `-march=native` if znver3 is unrecognized). `run` tees to `lulesh-run.log` and prints the full-precision elapsed value from the `( … overall)` field of the Grind time line, not the 2-sig-fig summary. Expect roughly 1–3 minutes of solve time.

Sources: [Frontier User Guide](https://docs.olcf.ornl.gov/systems/frontier_user_guide.html), [HPE Cray intro_hugepages](https://cpe.ext.hpe.com/docs/latest/craype/intro_hugepages.html)
